sections.heading: Provenance, Legislative Objective & Doctrinal Foundations
sections.body: This topic covers s. 172–179 under the Indian Contract Act, 1872. Read the statutory scheme as a coherent allocation of rights, duties, conditions, defences and consequences.

sections.body:

sections.heading: Evidentiary Burdens under BSA 2023 (ss. 104–106 & s. 63)
sections.body: The asserting party ordinarily bears the initial burden on essential facts, subject to admissions and statutory presumptions. Electronic records should be authenticated and presented under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023.

sections.body: Check jurisdiction, limitation, arbitration or jurisdiction clauses, court fees and the exact relief. Verify the applicable Limitation Act Article and accrual date.

enhancement.detailedExplanation:
India Code rule: Sections 172–179 define pledge, pawnor and pawnee and regulate retention, extraordinary expenses, sale on default, redemption, pledge by mercantile agents, pledge under voidable possession and limited-interest pledges.

Definition: A pledge is a bailment of goods as security for payment of a debt or performance of a promise, with the pawnee receiving statutory security rights.

Ingredients:
1. Identify pawnor, pawnee and the secured obligation.
2. Establish delivery or possession of the pledged goods as security.
3. Apply retention and expense rights.
4. On default, follow the statutory notice and sale rules.
5. Check the special rules for mercantile agents and limited interests.
examples: A pledges goods to B as security for a debt; on default B may exercise the statutory right to retain and, after complying with section 176, sell the pledged goods, subject to the pawnor’s right to redeem before sale.
problemApplication: Apply sections 172–179: identify the bailment or pledge, test the statutory duty/right, address the relevant exception, and conclude with the legal consequence.
